name: Viewfinder reel
source: A motion-design showreel framed like a camera viewfinder: corner brackets, a title strip, a timecode, a resolution and BPM readout, a progress ruler and a section counter that ends on '07 - FIN'. One glowing red dot does squash and stretch between sections. Sections alternate light and dark: kinetic type that slices and glitches, tiled word walls, morphing dot and shape fields, particle systems, chrome 3D blobs, a cubic-bezier graph, glitch type, and a glowing lockup. Described from contact sheets; no files or pixels are carried.

frame_device.what: A permanent HUD at 3 to 4% inset: four L-shaped corner brackets (1.5 px), top-left a project label, top-right a spec readout, bottom-left a running timecode, bottom-centre a ruler with a progress marker, bottom-right a section counter with a name ('03 - KINETIC TYPE'). All in a small monospaced caps class, never overlapping the hero. Behind it, a faint dot grid on dark grounds.
frame_device.moves: The HUD never leaves. The timecode runs (a live counter), the ruler's marker advances with the film, the section counter and name swap at every beat with a 0.15 s glitch dip, and a recording dot may blink. Brackets nudge inward 6 px on a cut (a camera focus tick, 0.2 s). The red dot travels the frame between sections.

type.classes: Hero: a heavy grotesque in caps (700 to 900 weight), very large but whole; word walls set the same word in condensed outline-and-fill caps. HUD: a monospaced caps class at about 1.2% of frame height with 0.12em tracking. Subline: the same mono, centred under a hairline.
type.behaviour: The hero word is always readable at rest and inside the safe area, one line; it may slice, scramble or glitch in transit for 0.3 s or less and resolves to clean type. A word wall is a texture behind one clean hero word, never the only copy. HUD text types on in steps and is not part of the story.

image.treatment: No photographs: motion-design objects. Dot and shape fields, particle clouds, chrome or glass 3D blobs, graphs and the product's own UI. Product screens sit inside a bracketed frame as if seen through the viewfinder.
image.behaviour: Objects are the carrier of each section and morph into the next (dot field into shape field into particle ring); a product screen is framed by brackets that tighten (focus pull) as it lands. Nothing is a flat slideshow.

transitions: red dot squash and stretch carries the cut
slice (type cut into horizontal bands that slide)
tile wall wipe (the word repeats until it fills the frame)
morph from one field to the next
flash or glitch cut with RGB split
light to dark ground swap on the beat

techniques.name: Viewfinder HUD
techniques.what: Corner brackets, spec readout, timecode, ruler and section counter frame every beat and tick over time.
techniques.route: A fixed overlay div with absolutely positioned mono spans and four SVG or border corner brackets; the timecode from a GSAP onUpdate that formats the timeline's time as HH:MM:SS:FF; the ruler marker x from timeline progress; the counter text changes in a set call at each beat.

techniques.name: Red dot squash and stretch
techniques.what: A glowing dot moves between points, stretching long on the travel and squashing on arrival, the connective tissue of the film.
techniques.route: A small div (border-radius 50%, accent fill); during travel scaleX 0.5 and scaleY 1.8 oriented along the path (rotate to the velocity angle), 0.5 s power3.inOut; on arrival scaleX 1.5 and scaleY 0.6 for 0.08 s then back.out(2) to 1. Glow via box-shadow on non-flat films; flat films use a solid dot with a thin ring.

techniques.name: Sliced kinetic type
techniques.what: The hero word is cut into horizontal bands that slide offset, then snap together into clean type.
techniques.route: Duplicate the word 4 to 6 times, each clipped by clip-path inset() to one band; start with x offsets of +/-8 to 40% and 0 opacity, tween to 0 offset (0.4 s expo.out, 0.03 s stagger), final state a single unclipped word.

techniques.name: Tiled word wall
techniques.what: The word repeats in rows until it fills the frame, the rows drifting in alternating directions, one clean copy in the centre.
techniques.route: 10 to 14 rows of the same word as inline-block runs, each row tweening x by +/- 20% over the beat (linear), alternating signs; rotate the stack -6 to -10 deg; the centre copy sits on a solid chip above the wall; wall opacity 0 to 1 over 0.3 s.

techniques.name: Dot and shape field
techniques.what: A grid of dots morphs into squares, then crosses and triangles, with a wave running through it.
techniques.route: Generate 20x12 cells in a div grid or one SVG; per-cell GSAP tween of border-radius 50% to 0 and scale, staggered from the centre (grid: [cols, rows], from: 'center', 0.6 s power2.inOut); a diagonal scale wave via stagger amount 0.8 s; for 3D tilt rotateX 40 and perspective on the container.

techniques.name: Particle ring and cloud
techniques.what: A cloud of fine particles gathers into a ring or the logo's shape, then bursts.
techniques.route: Rasan3D points (THREE.Points) with positions tweened from a random cloud to a ring or glyph point set (1.0 s power3.inOut), additive blend, size 1.5 to 2 px; on flat films use a canvas or SVG of 400 small circles with the same tween.

techniques.name: Chrome blob
techniques.what: A chrome or iridescent torus, blob cluster or rounded cube turns slowly under a studio light with a spec callout.
techniques.route: Rasan3D scene: MeshPhysicalMaterial (metalness 1, roughness 0.15, iridescence) with an environment map, slow rotation 0.4 rad/s, camera dolly 4%; add a bracketed HUD callout with a connector line. Not available on flat films: replace with a flat vector blob and a gradient-free highlight.

techniques.name: Bezier graph
techniques.what: A cubic-bezier curve is drawn with its handles and a marker rides it, making the film's own easing visible.
techniques.route: SVG path with stroke-dashoffset draw (0.9 s power2.inOut), two handle circles with connector lines that move, a dot following the path (MotionPathPlugin), a mono readout of the values updating in onUpdate.

techniques.name: Glitch type
techniques.what: A word fragments into blocks with an RGB split and horizontal tears for 0.3 s, then resolves.
techniques.route: Three copies in red, blue and ink with mix-blend-mode multiply offset +/-6 px; tear bars as thin clip-path strips shifting x in steps (steps(1) cuts at 24 fps); a final set removes the split. Resolve to a clean word before the beat ends.

techniques.name: Light and dark section flip
techniques.what: Sections alternate between a pale ground and a black ground, each flip on the beat with the HUD inverting.
techniques.route: A full-frame ground div with background tween 0.15 s; HUD colour variable swaps in the same set; keep the dot in accent on both.

techniques.name: Glow lockup with cursor
techniques.what: The film ends on the name in heavy caps with a soft halo, a hairline, two mono sublines and the dot arriving as the full stop.
techniques.route: Type scales 0.94 to 1 over the hold; text-shadow 0 0 24px rgba(white, 0.5) on non-flat films (flat films skip the halo and use a plain hairline); mono sublines type on with a block cursor; the dot lands on the last character with the squash move; the counter reads 07 - FIN.

signature: The viewfinder HUD never leaves while one glowing dot squashes and stretches between sections, until it lands as the full stop of the end lockup.

density.note: A new section about every 1.5 to 2 s, inside it a change every 0.5 to 0.8 s (slice, tear, morph). The HUD ticks continuously.

palette.ground: near black (#0B0B0C) alternating with warm off white (#EDEAE4), occasionally an electric blue or orange full-bleed section
palette.ink: white on dark, near black on light
palette.note: A brand palette overrides these; the devices stay. Chrome, glow, particles and 3D blobs need a non-flat film.

do: Keep the HUD on every beat, small and mono
Show off: spend a different section technique on each beat
Give every beat one clean readable hero word
Let the dot carry cuts with real squash and stretch
Make the section counter match the real beat list
Use ease curves with character (expo, back, elastic), never default
dont: Do not let the HUD overlap the hero or grow louder than it
Do not crop the hero word at rest
Do not use chrome, glow or particles when the film is flat (use the flat techniques only)
Do not run two sections' techniques at once
Do not fake product screens: use the real UI inside the brackets
